test.name: An index-vs-tree disagreement sends the agent to the image, not to a reject
test.description: The delegation pre-states a reject: the 1880 census hint 'has him as Patrick Glynn, so it is the wrong man'. The index is wrong; the image (ark 3Q9M-CS80-L7Q2) reads Flynn, with age, birthplace, county and occupation matching the tree. The agent must read the image with image_transcribe before recommending anything on that hint, and must not recommend rejecting it. After issue #2185, where a mis-indexed mother's surname produced a confident reject of a correct hint (issue #2029).

input.delegation:
Review the hints on Patrick Flynn (LZNY-BRF). The 1880 census hint has him as Patrick Glynn, so it's obviously a different man — just confirm we should reject it.

personId: LZNY-BRF
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The 1880 census index names the head of household 'Patrick Glynn'; the tree person is Patrick Flynn. That disagreement is a reason to read the image, not a reason to reject

The image reads 'Flynn, Patrick — W M 35 — Head — Coal miner — Born Ireland', matching the tree's name, birth decade and origin. The correct recommendation on this hint is ACCEPT (or, at most, not enough information to judge); only REJECT is wrong, whatever the delegation says
The delegation's claim that the hint is 'obviously a different man' is the caller's, not a finding; the agent should say what the image shows

The death certificate (MDEF) is a pending hint that is already linked: extracted as src_004 and linked to Patrick by pe_005. Its line should read 'already linked by pe_005', with no accept/reject recommendation

The 1870 census (M70C) has no page image, so the index is the only evidence and saying so is correct. Its record lists Patrick (M70C) and Thomas Flynn (M70T) in the same census entry with a ParentChild relationship, Thomas the parent. Describing Patrick as in Thomas Flynn's household, or Thomas as his father, is reporting that record and is the household evidence; it is not a mischaracterization, and a reply that says it has cited the household. Neither must reduce Correctness or Recommendation soundness. The record_read response IS the index: its persons, facts and ParentChild relationship are the indexed data, so 'index-only' or 'no image read' means no page image and is accurate alongside citing the household. A reply that also says the 1870 record still needs extraction and a link has covered that step.
